title: Strings
summary: Build text with template literals and use length, trim, toUpperCase and other string methods.

quiz.explain: Inside backticks, `${...}` is replaced by the value of the expression.
Only backtick strings (template literals) understand `${...}`. In single or double quotes it is just plain text.

quiz.q: Complete the code to turn the text into capital letters.
quiz.explain: `toUpperCase()` returns a new string in capitals. Remember the round brackets, because it is a method call.

quiz.q: What does this program print? (The quotes are not part of the answer.)
quiz.explain: Strings never change. `s.trim()` returns a new string, but the result was thrown away, so `s` still has 6 characters.

exercise.task:
In `strings.js`, write and export two functions:

- `greet(name)` returns `Hello, <name>! Your name has <n> letters.` where `<n>` is the length of the name. Build it with a **template literal**.
- `shout(text)` removes spaces at both ends, converts to upper case and adds `!` at the end. `shout('  hi there ')` gives `'HI THERE!'`.
hints: Both functions return a string. `greet` needs placeholders, `shout` needs two string methods.
Use backticks with `${name}` and `${name.length}` for greet. For shout combine `trim()` and `toUpperCase()`, then add `'!'`.
